title: Kṛṣṇa Meets Kubjā
adaptation_notice: Child-friendly adapted narration and dialogue; none is a verbatim quotation.
reflection: We can offer what we have with generosity, speak kindly, and treat every person with dignity. A person's worth is never measured by appearance.

panels.title: Mathurā's royal road
panels.visual: Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma walk the lively royal road of Mathurā.
panels.narration: In the great city of Mathurā, Kṛṣṇa and His elder brother Balarāma walked along the royal road, seeing the city and meeting its people. Around them, shopkeepers arranged colorful goods and neighbors greeted one another. The city felt busy and bright.

panels.title: A fragrant tray
panels.visual: Trivakrā, respectfully depicted, carries fragrant ointments on a tray.
panels.narration: On the road they met Trivakrā, also called Kubjā. She carried a tray of fragrant ointments she had prepared. Her careful work had brought a pleasant fragrance to the road, and the brothers noticed her tray.

panels.title: A friendly question
panels.visual: Kṛṣṇa speaks warmly to Trivakrā as Balarāma stands nearby.
panels.narration: Kṛṣṇa smiled and asked who the ointments were for. He asked whether she might share some with Him and Balarāma. He spoke in a playful and welcoming way, giving her room to answer freely.

dialogue.speaker: Kṛṣṇa
dialogue.text: Your tray smells lovely. Would you share some with us?

panels.title: Trivakrā's work
panels.visual: Trivakrā explains her work, holding the tray carefully.
panels.narration: Trivakrā explained that she served King Kaṁsa and was valued for making the ointments.

dialogue.speaker: Trivakrā
dialogue.text: I make these ointments in the king's service. Please accept them.

panels.title: A generous offering
panels.visual: Trivakrā willingly offers ointment to both brothers.
panels.narration: With a generous heart, Trivakrā offered a good amount of ointment to Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma. It was her willing gift.

panels.title: The brothers receive it
panels.visual: The brothers receive the ointment in a warm storybook scene.
panels.narration: The brothers accepted the fragrant cosmetics. The text describes how beautiful they looked adorned with the ointment. The story describes their appearance, not the value of any person standing beside them.

panels.title: A compassionate response
panels.visual: Kṛṣṇa gently helps Trivakrā stand upright in a dignified composition.
panels.narration: Pleased by her offering, Kṛṣṇa chose to help Trivakrā. The chapter describes Him placing His feet on her toes, lifting her chin, and straightening her body.

panels.title: A changed posture
panels.visual: Trivakrā stands upright, meeting others' gaze with a joyful expression.
panels.narration: By Kṛṣṇa's touch, Trivakrā's body became straight and balanced. She stood upright. Her dignity and worth had always been her own. Those watching could see a remarkable change, while Trivakrā remained the same person with her skills and generous spirit.

panels.title: An invitation
panels.visual: Trivakrā invites Kṛṣṇa to her home.
panels.narration: Trivakrā was joyful and invited Kṛṣṇa to visit her home. The original passage includes her strong longing; this child-friendly retelling keeps the invitation simple. Her invitation came after an unusual meeting, and Kṛṣṇa answered her directly and kindly.

dialogue.speaker: Trivakrā
dialogue.text: Please visit my home. I would be happy to welcome you.

panels.title: Kṛṣṇa replies
panels.visual: Kṛṣṇa replies while Balarāma and the cowherd boys look on.
panels.narration: Kṛṣṇa glanced at Balarāma and the cowherd boys, then answered with a laugh. He said He would come after completing His purpose.

dialogue.speaker: Kṛṣṇa
dialogue.text: I will visit after I have finished my work.

panels.title: A peaceful pause
panels.visual: The three share a peaceful moment on Mathurā's street before the scene fades.
panels.narration: The meeting comes to a gentle close. Trivakrā has shared what she made, and Kṛṣṇa has responded to her with care. It is a reminder that a sincere offering can begin a meaningful exchange between people.

panels.title: A reflection
panels.visual: A warm storybook closing view of the city and its people.
panels.narration: What can we learn? We can be generous, speak kindly, and honor every person's dignity. A person's worth is never measured by appearance.
